surface that owns it (the register, a checklist, the build plan, the questions) and
regenerate. `--check` fails when this file is stale, so the view cannot drift.

Priority is derived, not assigned: a register row of severity `halt`, an unrun hardware
step and a beta-gate build unit are P0; `spec` rows and remaining units are P1; design,
process, polish, open questions and coverage debt are P2.

| R-1008 | app-wide | register | spec **fixed** (`f4c1fd2e`, merged 2026-09-20): new `pushedtoastchannel` - a `channel(unlimited)` whose `push()` never suspends - collected by a `launchedeffect` in `failurehost` **alongside**, not instead of, the existing `sessionid`-keyed poll loop, so a result arriving mid-navigation is not missed. the choice of primitive is the substance and the builder argued it rather than following the codebase's habit: a plain mutable holder can drop a second push before the first is read (loses a result), while a `stateflow`/`sharedflow(replay=1)` re-delivers its last value to every new collector (shows a result twice); an unlimited channel gives both properties at once. `recoverytoast` gained a defaulted `onundo`, so all four existing polled call sites are unchanged. discriminated twice - `while(true)` to `while(false)` failed all four host cases; dropping the `onundo` pass-through failed exactly the undo case. **undo conclusion, recorded:** it can survive a destination change, but only by construction - the closure must be built from data the action's own result produced, captured by value at push time, never from an ambient current selection. nothing enforces that; see r-1139, which is the reason this is not yet wired to a real caller./fixed / awaiting capture | P4, `Feedback.dc.html` |

| R-1103 | The tour script itself has no test | register | process **fixed** (branch `m-tooling-provenance`, commit `<pending>`): followed `diff.py`'s own same-night precedent (r-1116) rather than introducing pester - the run-id-matching (`check_done_marker`) and fewer-results-than-requested (`verify_step_count`/`verify_pulled_count`) decisions, plus the manifest-line parsing both depended on (`summarize`), are now a plain python module, `tools/ui-audit/tour_manifest.py`, with no device dependency. `tour.ps1` was rewired to shell out to it for all three decisions rather than keep its own inline copy - a builder that only extracted the logic without wiring it in would have reproduced exactly the "built but not connected" pattern this register is full of. new suite `tools/ui-audit/tests/test_tour_manifest.py` (19 cases) is picked up automatically by the existing `ui-audit-diff` ci job (`pytest tools/ui-audit -q`), no new job needed. the discriminating case this row names -
